findings.title: Pressure crosses the collective limit
findings.claim: The focus's failure of mutual restraint can also be seen as excess pressing past a stopping point: the wrong remains in motion because the boundary that should end it is not enforced.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier يَتَنَاهَوْنَ supplies reciprocal restraint, while 5:73 supplies reaching an endpoint and 5:77 supplies غ ل و as excess, boiling, and farthest reach. Their contact turns the focus from a static report of omitted admonition into a bounded image of pressure crossing a limit and continuing.
findings.reader_payoff: The social failure gains a dynamic shape: what should have been stopped gathers force, passes its appointed edge, and remains attached to the group's conduct.
findings.containment: The ordinary meaning remains the report that they did not mutually forbid the wrong they committed. Boiling and arrow-range are supplied analogies for pressure and limit; no literal heat, arrow, or whole-surah system is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The trusted candidate supplies the focus and pericope relations, the exact 5:77 carrier, and the bounded pressure-crossing synthesis.

findings.title: Affiliation leaves no corrective gap
findings.claim: The focus's failure to mutually restrain a rejected wrong can also be read as a maintained social proximity: affiliation and adopted alliance leave no corrective gap, carry the practice forward, and attach its consequence to the participants.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies mutual restraint and the rejected wrong, while the attributed 5:80-81 coordinates supply affiliation, forward advancement, self-reception, lasting attachment, deliberate adoption, and nearness. Their contact revises silence from empty passivity into a possible social alignment that helps the wrong persist.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how failing to interrupt a wrong may itself preserve the relation that carries it: closeness, support, and adopted alliance become the medium of continuation.
findings.containment: The focus still plainly condemns the wrong and the failure to restrain it. This attributed pericope reading does not make affiliation the only explanation; it preserves the live alternative that 5:80-81 are adjacent charges rather than the focus's mechanism.

epistemic.reason: The HFT record provides complete exact anchors, before/after reading, and focus return, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and six context branch records are unresolved.

findings.title: Action has no settling basin
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the focus's repeated wrongdoing can be pictured as action entering a flow with no settling basin: reciprocal restraint never gives it a terminal place to stop, while later overflow and river imagery supply movement and capacity.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries the supplied stream-end and repeated-action facets; 5:83 contributes overflow and a filled vessel, and 5:85 contributes running water and rivers. Their contact changes the focus's missing restraint into a material analogy for uncontained action without changing the ordinary moral report.
findings.reader_payoff: The phrase about not restraining wrongdoing gains a physical intuition: the acts keep entering the stream, pressure accumulates, and nothing provides the basin in which motion can settle.
findings.containment: The focus still says that they did not mutually forbid the wrong they had done. This exploratory model is anchored in the supplied HFT trace and its exact focus return; it is not a lexical translation of يَتَنَاهَوْنَ and does not claim that the later water imagery is the focus's literal subject.

epistemic.reason: The trace supplies complete exact coordinates and an explicit material-analogy boundary, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound, its context morphology is not independently supplied, and the source labels the result exploratory.
